item.title: Recent theoretical and computational developments on infinite Bayesian mixtures — Fri Sep 4, 3:30 PM — Old Chemistry 116
item.description:
Mixture models driven by a Dirichlet process are among the most widely used tools in Bayesian nonparametric statistics, yet fundamental questions about both their inferential behaviour and their scalability to large datasets remain open. In this talk I present recent progress on both fronts.
On the theoretical side, I study the asymptotic behaviour of the posterior on the mixing measure when the data are truly generated by a finite mixture. The posterior turns out to be adaptive to the unknown number of components: the mass it places on the superfluous atoms of the stick-breaking representation vanishes at a near-parametric rate, yielding a nearly optimal contraction rate for the mixing measure in Wasserstein distance. item.description:
Propaganda is one of the oldest concepts associated with global communication. Used for centuries to influence public opinion and shape political outcomes, propaganda continues to play a significant role in both domestic and international politics.
In today's highly interconnected world, where communication technologies and patterns of human interaction are rapidly evolving, Dr. Yahya R. Kamalipour, editor of the recently published book Propaganda in the Digital Age: Global Conflicts, Media, Politics, and Fake News, offers a multifaceted examination of propaganda and its contemporary manifestations.
The presentation explores the complex relationships among propaganda, war, media, information, misinformation, and disinformation, with particular attention to how digital technologies have transformed the production, dissemination, and consumption of political messages. item.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star (Theatre for the Very Young) — Wed Sep 9, 10:00 AM — Raleigh Little Theatre
item.description:
Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star is an interactive children’s theatre piece for very young audiences, performed by two Star Keepers named Glimmer and Sparkle. It’s time for the night sky to fill with stars, but one important star — Little Star, the wishing star — is missing because Sparkle rushed through putting the stars away the previous morning and muddled everything up. What follows is a search-and-rescue adventure as the two star keepers (and the audience) hunt for Little Star, discovering along the way that all the other stars have been put in the wrong places too and need to be moved to their proper place. Audience members help the Star Keepers find and re-organize the sky just in time for nightfall so that everyone can make a wish on their favorite star. Twinkle, Twinkle explores the ideas that mistakes happen, feelings are valid, and no one has to face hard things alone – all wrapped up in a genuinely joyful romp about stars.
